headline: Boat Transfer and Island Access Permits Required
reservation: National Park entry fees must be paid through the SÉPAQ website or at the Percé visitor office. Cruising to Île Bonaventure requires a separate ticket purchased from private boat operators at the Percé wharf. These boat departures are weather-dependent and do not include the park entry fee; ensure you have both the SÉPAQ permit and a boat boarding pass before heading to the dock.

days.title: The Gannet Colony of Bonaventure

stops.name: Les Colonies Trail
stops.detail: Walk across the island to witness one of the world's largest Northern Gannet colonies in their natural nesting grounds.

stops.name: Chemin-du-Roy
stops.detail: Follow the coastal perimeter path to see historic island homes and rugged cliffs facing the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

days.driving: No vehicle access on the island; local boat transfer takes approximately 45 minutes including a loop of Rocher Percé.
days.note: The last boat leaves the island in the late afternoon; check the daily schedule posted at the island dock.

days.title: Percé Rock and Coastal Heritage

stops.name: Mont-Joli Lookout
stops.detail: Gain an elevated view of the iconic pierced rock and the historical Charles Robin fishing buildings below.

stops.name: Percé UNESCO Global Geopark
stops.detail: Visit the glass platform at the Geopark for a vertical perspective of the coastline's unique tectonic history.

days.driving: Local walking within Percé village; allow 20 minutes for the hike up to the Geopark platform.
days.note: Walking to the base of Percé Rock is extremely dangerous and often prohibited due to frequent rockfalls.

days.title: Gaspesian Headlands

stops.name: Emerald River (Rivière aux Émeraudes)
stops.detail: A short drive from Percé to see the strikingly clear green waters and waterfall in the nearby forest.

stops.name: Cap-d'Espoir
stops.detail: Visit the lighthouse area for expansive views of the Gulf and potential whale sightings from the shore.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes for the return trip to Cap-d'Espoir; roads are paved but winding.
days.note: River access may involve steep stairs; check local conditions for water clarity after heavy rains.

intel.title: Village and Wharf Zones
intel.text: Parking in Percé is mostly paid and managed by the municipality or private lots. During the peak summer season, arrive early to secure a spot near the wharf as central lots fill by mid-morning.

intel.title: Island and Coastal Reach
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong in Percé village and on the high points of Île Bonaventure. However, reception can be blocked by the cliffs on the seaward side of the island.

intel.title: Gaspé Peninsula Supply
intel.text: Gas stations are available in Percé and nearby Grande-Rivière. If driving the full Gaspé Peninsula loop, keep your tank above half as distances between larger service centers can be significant.

intel.title: Boat Departure Windows
intel.text: Boats generally run from late May to early October. High winds or heavy fog in the Gulf of St. Lawrence can cancel all departures with little notice; plan a buffer day if possible.

intel.title: Island Footpaths
intel.text: Bonaventure Island is accessible only by boat and features well-maintained but gravel-surfaced hiking trails. Sturdy walking shoes are required for the 5.6km to 9km loops depending on the chosen route.

plan.arrival: Fly into Gaspé Airport (YGP) and drive 60 minutes south to Percé. Pick up groceries in Gaspé as the village selection is smaller.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for the Gaspé highway; parking large RVs in central Percé is difficult during peak hours.
plan.goldenHour: Mont-Joli provides the classic sunset silhouette of Rocher Percé, though the rock itself is best lit by the morning sun.
